answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph, so an identity gains influence through supported paths, not merely by multiplying accounts. A sybil cluster with a shale-like, low-conductance boundary leaks little trust to honest nodes; conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore limit its aggregate voting weight by the scarce external attestations anchoring it. Even a sonnet of mutual claims cannot turn an ember of connectivity into broad, independent trust.
